authority: Author-approved structural canon for next revision; no existing prose rewritten. Exact timing and mechanisms are provisional where noted.

architecture.form: Hybrid chronicle and independent character POV scenes
architecture.length: Let narrative find its natural length
architecture.process: Collect and assess authorial plot changes before restructuring

requests.title: Elias formative education
requirements: Plausible training in strategy, tactics, surveying, geology, mechanics and classical history
Retired colonel/engineer mentor, books including Plutarch, practical experience
Demonstrate memory, curiosity, stamina and ability to learn; allow genuine errors
Elias born circa 1824; his mentor may be a French emigré military engineer from Napoleon's era, versed in Vauban, Jomini, Plutarch and geology; 'colonel' rank possibly honorific or self-awarded.
Mentor introduces terrain reading and geological reasoning; Elias's talent is demonstrated through fallible real experiences, not assertions.
open: French mentor's name, exact service and verification of his claimed rank
Specific books and later role in Elias's life

requests.title: Elias temperament and belief
requirements: Animal affinity and exceptional horsemanship alongside hunting and ruthless self-defense
Night hikes and geological observation tied causally to prospecting
Nuanced religious heterodoxy; childhood incident with pastor and later marriage recommendation
His talents create vulnerabilities and moral contradiction
Boy Elias observes Big Bone Lick's fossil evidence and disputes biblical chronology; pastor strikes him first and Elias breaks his nose in retaliation.
Pastor's supposed later encouragement of his daughter to marry Elias must remain unverifiable early Chronicler testimony.
open: Pastor's identity and specific confrontation circumstances
Pastor's daughter's identity and reliability of her later story

requests.title: Founding friendships and agency
requirements: Dramatize first friendship with Caleb Vance through reciprocal dependence
Give peers and partners independent agendas and competence
Replace or repurpose early non sequitur bandit episodes
Elias aged about sixteen witnesses the March 1840 Council House Fight and learns the consequence of violated diplomatic safe conduct.
Elias and Caleb participate in the 1841–42 Texan Santa Fe Expedition, endure capture and the march to Mexico, bond through mutual dependence; Elias learns Spanish and makes Mexican contacts.

requests.title: Elias–Kaiulani family tragedy
requirements: They marry with genuine affection and joint political ambition
Their son dies in an accident; Kaiulani is subsequently unable to have more children
Their relationship deteriorates through loss, geopolitical conflicts, ambition and unresolved attachment
Elias has affairs and additional children
A younger Hawaiian-American woman, potentially a caretaker, becomes Julian's biological mother during Elias's final years
After Elias dies in 1887, Julian's mother dies under suspicious circumstances; Kaiulani's possible involvement remains uncertain
Kaiulani adopts infant/young Julian and raises him as her son
Kaiulani remains an ambitious political actor, not reduced to motherhood or jealousy
Julian grows up with genuine alternatives and conflicting loyalties, later leading the Restoration
Julian's age in the 1931 Restoration changes from 32 to about 44–45 if born about 1886–87
Kaiulani born 1838, a fictional cousin of Hawaiian princes; marriage to Elias occurs in Honolulu in 1857 after Alexander's 1856 marriage.
Kaiulani may hold Kuhina Nui or equivalent co-executive role through explicit divergence from historical incumbent Victoria Kamamalu.

Lot Kapuaiwa's death in December 1872 and the 1873–74 Hawaiian succession turmoil provide the preferred political setting for incorporation and a 1874 royalist massacre, not a unilateral naval-lease denial.
The shared legitimate child's death and Kaiulani's resulting inability to bear children occur after the relationship is established; exact date after 1874 remains provisional.
open: Legitimate child's identity, temperament, birth year and accident date/mechanism
Kaiulani's exact constitutional appointment relative to historical Victoria Kamamalu
Medical nature of infertility and certainty
Whether any of Elias's relationships and older sons predate the lost child's death, given adult claimants in 1887
Young Hawaiian-American mother's name, age, independent career, death and evidence for competing explanations
Julian's infancy, adoption, youth and estrangement
Precise genealogy for the 1914 Emperor Kalanimoku and other claimants
Hawaiian royalist parties, incorporation law and casualty figures in 1874

requests.title: Japanese diplomatic opening
requirements: Use Japanese castaways and Nakahama Manjiro, including Eiriki Maru/Joseph Heco, as early personal contacts
Enter through Ryukyu/Satsuma and Shimazu Nariakira, then negotiate with Abe Masahiro and shogunate
California initially promises limited trade, technical support, no missionaries and no territorial ambitions
Military and commercial reciprocity; Japanese factions independent and competent
Potential conflict over gold/silver valuation and growing asymmetry
Manjiro meets Elias during 1849–50 California stay; he returns through Ryukyu in 1851 to Satsuma/Shimazu Nariakira's scrutiny.
Eiriki Maru castaways reach California in 1851; California sends some home via Naha 1852–53, without forcing Joseph Heco's own historical return forward.
1854–55 Satsuma technical exchanges and Shimoda agreement; after Abe Masahiro dies 1857 and Nariakira 1858, political support changes under Ii Naosuke.
California warns shogunate of gold/silver arbitrage before post-1859 outflow; exchange ratio historically ~1:5 in Japan vs ~1:15 abroad.
Kanrin Maru arrives San Francisco 1860 with Manjiro aboard; a formal Edo agreement is signed. Early Japanese military cooperation limited to naval training and observers.
open: Specific technical agreements and plenipotentiaries
How Perry's actual 1853–54 expedition is credibly affected without an impossible universal coaling embargo
1857–60 Japanese monetary reform response and court faction politics

requests.title: American wars credibility
requirements: Competent Union and Confederate opposition; significant Pacifican defeat and casualties
Technology limited by industry, supply, geography, maintenance
Meaningful diplomacy, foreign partnerships, political compromise and adversary adaptation
Conquest of Washington not sufficient alone to dissolve federal institutions
Retain slavery and civil-war legitimacy as major political considerations

Elias opposes chattel slavery as damaging to independent labor, smallholders and civic institutions, shaped partly by his reading of the Gracchi; he is not an evangelical or humanitarian abolitionist.
Early Japanese military role limited to advisers, trainees and observers; substantial foreign involvement in American wars must be individually justified.
open: Campaign-level military and constitutional chronology

requests.title: Gold–industry–state power
requirements: Gold discovered by rigorous investigation informed by geological expertise and local knowledge
Gold openly known, government-regulated, not secretly mined for four years
Distinguish total extraction, public reserves and Elias's wealth
Plausible licensing, royalties, mines, mint, banking, credit and industrial scaling
Historic 1842 Placerita Canyon gold find informs prospecting, rather than Elias being the first to know California has gold.
Proposed spring 1848 southern Mother Lode discovery around Stanislaus/Mokelumne with Elias, Caleb, skilled Sonoran miner and Miwok/Yokuts guide; indigenous and Mexican partners retain agency.
California applies and adapts Spanish/Mexican 1783 Mining Ordinances with registration, concessions, revenue and contested private surface rights; no automatic confiscation of all gold.
open: Final precise stream and proven deposit
Names and agendas of Sonoran miner and Miwok/Yokuts guide
Mining claim registry, exact royalty rates, ownership and public finance

requests.title: Independent California before US statehood
requirements: California republic founded around 1845–1846 and never joins the US
Political coalition includes Californios, settlers and autonomous Indigenous communities with independent interests
1848 gold legally managed by sovereign California, with public rush and manageable revenues
British commercial/diplomatic support plausible but not an automatic military guarantee
Directly account for U.S. naval operations in 1846 and international legitimacy
Replace 1852 territorial admission/secession with constitutional consolidation
Elias arrives 1844 and supports Alvarado/Castro against Micheltorena and Sutter; the February 1845 battle of Providencia gives him political standing.
Coalition founders include Alvarado, Castro and Pico, but real divisions between Pico and Castro in 1846 must be reconciled in the fictional convention.
Vallejo remains a credible pro-American internal dissenter; Sem-Yeto/Solano of Suisun represents particular indigenous interests rather than an all-tribes mandate.
Founding constitutional convention accelerated from historical June 15 1846 Santa Barbara plan to spring 1846 before war news; California never joins USA.
Commodore Sloat's 1842 Jones precedent and 1846 hesitation, HMS Collingwood's arrival July 16 and the threat posed by Fremont's irregulars form the naval crisis.
Mexico recognizes independence against assumption of part of its London debt; British creditor support need not imply naval protection.
1850 Sacramento squatter conflict and 1851 San Francisco vigilance crisis lead to 1852 constitutional reorganization.
Elias is not head of state in 1852, serving as Superintendent of Mines and Public Revenue or equivalent, with Alvarado/Castro or other elected constitutional leader remaining president.
open: Exact date of spring 1846 constitutional convention and founding laws
Californio coalition negotiating process, especially Pico/Castro hostility
Terms of Sloat/Fremont crisis and 1846 peace without US annexation
Indigenous negotiated rights and leadership
Terms of British creditor/Mexican recognition settlement and cash flow
Exact 1852 presidency and Elias's ministry

explicit_cautions: Do not give the dead legitimate child no individuality; portray him as a real person before the accident.
Do not make infertility or jealousy the sole motive for Kaiulani's subsequent decisions.
Do not reduce the younger mother to a reproductive plot device; she must have her own agency.
Do not assert Kaiulani murdered Julian's mother without deliberate later authorization; preserve genuine ambiguity.
Do not make Julian's later politics genetically or psychologically inevitable, or predetermine his character.
Preserve Kaiulani's independent statecraft, political ambitions, and complicity in imperial decisions.
No technological miracles or effortlessly incompetent opposition.
Authorial change requests are authoritative; editorial implementations beyond them remain proposals.
Keep the current master storyline a continuous affirmative narrative, without comparisons to old manuscript construction; put research and implementation notes in historical_background.md.

Distinguish verified historical events from fictional divergences, particularly Pico-Castro reconciliation, spring 1846 convention, Sloat's delayed response, British debt support and the 1874 Hawaiian massacre.
Kaiulani born 1838 is fictional, not Victoria Kamamalu or Princess Victoria Kaiulani; assign Kuhina Nui through an explicit alternate historical event.
Lot Kapuaiwa dies December 1872; move Hawaiian centralization/massacre toward 1874 to integrate succession, not earlier 1867.
Respect the age arithmetic of Elias 1824, Kaiulani 1838, 1857 wedding, 1887 Elias death, Julian c.1886–87 birth and 1931 mid-forties Restoration.
The timing of Silas/Kiyoshi and the legitimate son's loss must remain open rather than making adult succession leaders impossibly young.
No automatic assumption that Japan's Perry mission vanishes solely because California has purchased coal contracts.
The 1783 mining ordinances do not settle contested private titles or the rights of Indigenous peoples without state law and negotiation.

provisional_timeline.event: Birth of Elias Thorne in Kentucky.
French émigré Napoleonic engineering mentor; Big Bone Lick geology dispute with pastor; foreclosure 1837.
At age 16 Elias witnesses the Council House Fight and its consequences.
Santa Fe Expedition captures Elias and Caleb; march to Mexico and imprisonment create enduring friendship and Spanish competence.
Elias arrives in California and supports Californio revolt against Micheltorena; battle of Providencia.
Pico/Castro/Alvarado coalition negotiates founding convention at Santa Barbara; independent republic declared before the US-Mexican war news dominates.
Sloat's naval hesitation, Fremont irregular conflict, Collingwood's arrival, British creditor interests and Mexico's debt-for-recognition settlement.
Visible public gold discovery near Stanislaus or Mokelumne; inherited Spanish/Mexican mineral regime governs claims and royalties.
Hawaiian princes visit California; friendship of Elias with Lot, Alexander as political partner. Elias meets Manjiro.
Sacramento squatter conflict, San Francisco vigilance crisis; Manjiro returns via Ryukyu/Satsuma, Eiriki Maru castaways reach California.
Constitutional reorganization: Elias becomes Superintendent of Mines and Public Revenue, not President; Californian repatriation mission through Naha.
California and Satsuma technical exchanges; Shimoda agreement and shogunal diplomacy.
Elias and Kaiulani marry in Honolulu. Abe Masahiro dies; Japanese foreign policy enters a more precarious phase.
Nariakira dies; Ii Naosuke's political ascendancy, Ansei purge and emerging gold outflow risk.
Kanrin Maru reaches San Francisco; Manjiro interprets; Edo agreement becomes formal foundation of partnership.
Pacifica's war with capable Union and Confederate adversaries; substantial losses, diplomacy and political settlement.
Alaska/Yukon, Spanish possessions, revised Edo negotiation, campaigns in China, Bering and Siberia; Marcus Vance I dies.
Lot dies December 1872; Hawaiian succession crisis and imperial incorporation culminate in royalist suppression and massacre c.1874.
Elias and Kaiulani's legitimate son dies in an accident that leaves Kaiulani unable to bear children; date and details open.
Affairs, other children, political divisions and construction of mature imperial systems.
Young Hawaiian-American woman becomes Elias's lover, potentially caretaker; Julian born c.1886–87.
Elias dies; succession crisis begins.
Julian's mother dies under suspicious circumstances; Kaiulani adopts and raises Julian; Truce of Thalassia 1888.
Kaiulani's regency and Julian's upbringing; technocratic consolidation; Panama Canal completion 1900.
Dynastic settlement through alternate line of Elias; exact Kalanimoku genealogy open.
India, Europe, Afghanistan, empire overstretch and Kaiulani's renunciation.
Labor revolt, automation, anti-imperial movements, collapse of Vance III.
Julian's Restoration, arrest of Kaiulani, final collapse and Chronicler's escape.

approval_sync.requirements: Each explicit author approval must update the relevant authored chronological narrative in master_storyline.md and change_requests.json together.
approval_sync.generated_ledger: The approved_change_index.md administrative record is generated deterministically from this registry, separately from the continuous storyline.
approval_sync.validation: GitHub PR checks run sync_master_storyline.py --check for exact index sync and presence of approved CR coverage IDs in master_storyline.md.
approval_sync.limits: Neither automatic ledger sync nor a coverage-ID check proves substantive prose integration; each approval requires editorial review of changed narrative paragraphs.
